doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20734-w.abstract: Ischemic reperfusion injury (IRI) during liver transplantation is associated with recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Machine perfusion (MP) is associated with a decreased risk of IRI complications. Our study evaluated the role of MP in post-transplant oncologic outcomes in patients with HCC. Adults with HCC transplanted between 2015-2025 from the United Network for Organ Sharing database were divided into MP and no-MP groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) was also performed. Post-transplant HCC recurrence (competing risk) and overall survival (OS) were assessed. Subgroup analysis was performed in populations within and beyond the Milan criteria. A total of 19,466 patients were included in this study. MP was used in 1,392 (7.2%). The MP group had shorter waitlist times, older donors, and more frequent DCDs (p=0.001). After PSM, 512 patients were included in each group (336 patients within Milan criteria in each). In the population beyond Milan after PSM (n=352), MP use was associated with a reduced risk of 1-year and 3-year HCC recurrence (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.09, p=0.02; aHR 0.27, p=0.02). MP use was not associated with the 1-year or 3-year OS (aHR 1.34, p=0.64; aHR 1.32, p=0.54). MP may potentially reduce the risk of HCC recurrence in recipients beyond Milan criteria, without significant difference in OS. However, as MP utilization increases, further validation into the role of MP and oncologic outcomes in larger cohort studies are required.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20735-9.abstract: Contemporary gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEPNET) management guidelines recommend routine use of functional imaging preoperatively, but there are few data highlighting trends in functional imaging adoption. This report reviews 24 years of neuroendocrine tumor (NET) experience to describe changes in rates of preoperative functional imaging use and highlights performance differences between functional imaging types in small bowel NETs (SBNET) and pancreatic NETs (PNETs). A retrospective single-institution study from 2000 to 2023 identified patients with SBNETs and PNETs treated with surgical resection, cytoreduction, or both who underwent preoperative functional imaging. The primary measurements were frequency of functional imaging use and location of metastases identified on preoperative imaging. The study included 392 SBNET and 208 PNET patients. Preoperative functional imaging was performed for 248 (63.3%) SBNET patients (158 somatostatin receptor [SSTR] positron emission tomography [PET] and 90 Octreoscan) and 113 (54.3%) PNET patients (47 SSTR PET and 66 Octreoscan). There was a significant positive trend over time in functional imaging use in SBNET patients, with an approximate 2.5% yearly increase (p < 0.01) but no significant change in PNET patients during the course of the study (p = 0.82). At presentation, 82.3% (204/248) of the SBNET patients and 54.9% (62/113) of the PNET patients had metastatic disease. Compared with Octreoscan, SSTR PET more frequently identified bone and retroperitoneal nodal metastases. Rates of functional imaging use in SBNET patients but not in PNET patients increased significantly during the last 24 years. Patients with SBNETs and PNETs frequently presented with metastatic disease, and SSTR-based functional imaging was extremely helpful in identifying distant disease, intra-operative planning, and further management.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20736-8.abstract: Reliable biomarkers for predicting tumor aggressiveness and pathological upstaging in renal cell carcinoma (RCC) remain limited. DR-70, a biomarker reflecting circulating fibrin and fibrin degradation products, has been associated with tumor progression in several malignancies. This study aimed to investigate the association between preoperative serum DR-70 levels and pathological stage and nuclear grade in patients with localized RCC. This prospective single-center study included 69 patients who underwent partial or radical nephrectomy for localized RCC. Tumors were staged according to the TNM classification and graded using the World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology system. Preoperative serum DR-70 levels were measured, and their associations with clinical stage, pathological stage, and nuclear grade were evaluated. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of pathological upstaging (≥ pT3). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was used to assess the predictive performance of DR-70. The median serum DR-70 level was 0.84 U/mL. DR-70 levels were significantly higher in high-grade tumors than in low-grade tumors (1.32 vs. 0.78 U/mL, p = 0.001). No significant association was observed between DR-70 levels and clinical stage (p = 0.53), whereas a significant association was found with pathological stage (p = 0.023). Multivariate analysis identified serum DR-70 as an independent predictor of pathological upstaging (≥ pT3) (odds ratio 1.40; 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.81; p = 0.008). Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated good predictive performance for high-grade disease (area under the curve 0.823) and pathological upstaging (area under the curve 0.774), with an optimal cutoff value of 1.02 U/mL. Serum DR-70 was associated with tumor aggressiveness and independently predicted pathological upstaging in patients with localized RCC. These findings suggest that DR-70 may serve as a complementary biomarker for preoperative risk stratification and may help identify patients at increased risk of aggressive pathological features. Larger multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings.

doi:10.1245/s10434-026-20765-3.abstract: Conventional survival analyses cannot fully account for recurrence as an intermediate event that dynamically influences subsequent mortality. Multistate models (MSMs) enable explicit modeling of transitions between clinically relevant disease states; however, their application among patients undergoing resection for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) remains limited. An international multi-institutional database was queried to identify patients undergoing curative-intent hepatectomy for CRLM between 1998 and 2023. A four-state MSM was constructed comprising alive and recurrence-free, alive with recurrence, colorectal cancer (CRC)-related death, and non-CRC-related death. Transition probabilities and transition-specific prognostic factors were evaluated RESULTS: Among 3002 patients, 1624 (54.1%) developed recurrence and 911 (56.1%) died, predominantly from CRC-related causes (92.8%). The probability of recurrence decreased substantially the longer patients remained recurrence-free after surgery, whereas recurrence markedly worsened subsequent prognosis. High tumor burden score was independently associated with transition to recurrence (hazard ratio [HR] 1.06 per unit; 95% confidence interval 1.03-1.08; p < 0.001) but not post-recurrence mortality, suggesting that the adverse prognostic impact of tumor burden was mediated primarily through recurrence. Adjuvant chemotherapy reduced recurrence (HR 0.76; p = 0.005) and CRC-related death from the recurrence-free state (HR 0.39; p = 0.002). MSMs provide a dynamic framework to characterize disease evolution after CRLM resection and represent recurrence as a clinically meaningful time-dependent intermediate state rather than a simple binary endpoint. Recurrence was the dominant determinant of long-term prognosis, supporting the role of MSMs for individualized prognostication and surveillance after hepatectomy for CRLM.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1768933.abstract: Malnutrition, altered body composition, and sarcopenia are common among patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and are associated with poor treatment tolerance and adverse clinical outcomes. PhA, derived from BIA, reflects cellular membrane integrity and body cell mass and has been increasingly investigated as a potential marker of nutritional status and prognosis in oncology. However, the clinical relevance of PhA in patients with CRC has not yet been systematically synthesized. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for observational studies published between January 2000 and October 2025 that assessed PhA in adult patients with CRC. Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the AXIS tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study design, outcome definitions, and PhA cut-off values, a narrative synthesis was conducted. A total of 10 studies involving 1,439 patients were included. Lower PhA values were consistently associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Four studies reported significantly shorter overall or progression-free survival among patients with low PhA. Four studies demonstrated associations between low PhA and unfavorable short-term outcomes, including postoperative complications, prolonged hospital stay, cancer-related complications, and early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Several studies also reported positive associations between PhA and indicators of nutritional status, body composition, muscle mass, muscle strength, and hydration balance. One longitudinal study showed that postoperative increases in PhA were accompanied by improvements in body composition parameters and reduced early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Current evidence indicates that BIA-derived phase angle is associated with nutritional status, body composition, treatment tolerance, and survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer. However, heterogeneity in measurement protocols and cut-off values limits direct clinical application. Standardized assessment methods and prospective studies are needed to establish CRC-specific reference values and to determine whether interventions that improve PhA can translate into improved clinical outcomes.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1773440.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that oral microbiota dysbiosis and periodontal pathogens contribute to the initiation and progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the interaction between Porphyromonas gingivalis and the tumor immune microenvironment remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the potential role of a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling pathway in P. gingivalis-mediated immunosuppressive microenvironment formation during OSCC progression. Genes associated with P. gingivalis and TIGIT were obtained from GeneCards and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) databases. Candidate hub genes were identified through bioinformatic analyses. An SCC7 syngeneic orthotopic transplantation mouse model was established, and SCC7 cells were injected together with Porphyromonas gingivalis. Tumor growth was assessed by measuring tumor volume and weight. Expression levels of TLR4, ERK1/2, CD155, and TIGIT were evaluated by immunohistochemistry and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Flow cytometry was performed to analyze tumor-infiltrating immune-cell populations. The TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242 was used to investigate the involvement of TLR4-associated signaling. Bioinformatic analysis identified TLR4 as a biologically relevant candidate hub gene potentially linking P. gingivalis-associated signaling and TIGIT-related immune regulation. Exposure to P. gingivalis significantly promoted tumor growth and increased the expression of TLR4, ERK1/2, CD155, and TIGIT in tumor tissues. Flow cytometric analysis revealed immune microenvironment remodeling characterized by increased proportions of CD4+ T cells, TIGIT-positive Tregs, and IL-10-positive cells, accompanied by reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and decreased frequencies of Ki67+CD8+ and CD44+CD8+ T cells. Treatment with the TLR4 inhibitor TAK-242 partially reversed these tumor-promoting, immunological, and molecular changes. Our findings suggest that exposure to P. gingivalis may promote OSCC progression by contributing to immune microenvironment remodeling. Increased expression of TLR4, ERK1/2, CD155, and TIGIT, together with the effects of TLR4 inhibition, supports the potential involvement of a TLR4-associated ERK/CD155/TIGIT signaling pathway in this process. However, the precise molecular mechanisms require further validation using genetic and functional approaches.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1794020.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has become an increasingly popular tool in cancer care over the years. It shows promise in areas like pain management, psychological support, surgical training, and rehabilitation. Even though more studies are being done, there has not been a thorough analysis of the research trends in this field. This study looks at how VR interventions in cancer research have evolved over the past two decades, identifies research hotspots, and explores future directions. We collected publications related to VR in cancer research from the Web of Science Core Collection and Pubmed, covering the period from 2005 to 2025. Using VOSviewer and CiteSpace software, we performed bibliometric and visual analyses. These included examining publication trends, contributions by countries and institutions, author collaboration networks, journal impact, keyword co-occurrence, and citation bursts. A total of 1,259 publications from 110 countries were included. The number of publications fluctuated over time but generally increased, reaching its highest point in 2024 with 184 articles. The United States and China were the most active countries. Jordan had the highest average number of citations per paper. Among institutions, McGill University published the most papers, followed by the University of Toronto. The most productive journal was Surgical Endoscopy and Other Interventional Techniques, whilst Cancers and Supportive Care in Cancer showed the fastest growth. Main research themes included pain management, anxiety reduction, breast cancer, and surgical training. Emerging trends involve the combination of augmented reality (AR), digital health, and artificial intelligence (AI) with VR. This study shows that VR research in cancer care is expanding worldwide, with most contributions coming from North America and Europe. Pain management remains the most common application. New technologies such as AR, AI, and telemedicine are becoming more integrated into VR interventions.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1796519.abstract: Atypical spindle cell lipomatous tumor (ASCLT) is a rare benign adipocytic neoplasm, and primary involvement of the retroperitoneum is exceedingly uncommon. Because its imaging features overlap with those of other fat-containing tumors, particularly atypical lipomatous tumor/well-differentiated liposarcoma (ALT/WDL), preoperative diagnosis remains challenging. We report a case of primary retroperitoneal ASCLT in a 58-year-old woman whose lesion was incidentally detected during a routine physical examination. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a small, well-defined fat-containing mass located between the celiac trunk and the superior mesenteric artery, with fat-related signal attenuation on fat-suppressed sequences, no obvious diffusion restriction, and mild reticular enhancement after contrast administration. Complete surgical excision was performed, and postoperative histopathological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings supported the diagnosis of ASCLT, with no MDM2 amplification. Compared with previously reported retroperitoneal ASCLT cases, the present case provides detailed CT and multiparametric MRI findings for a small, incidentally detected lesion adjacent to major abdominal vessels. Recognition of this imaging pattern may help include ASCLT in the preoperative differential diagnosis and support appropriate surgical planning, while definitive diagnosis still requires pathological and molecular confirmation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1800218.abstract: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer incidence and mortality among women worldwide, with ongoing challenges in early detection, accurate diagnosis, prognosis estimation, and treatment-response assessment. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, has rapidly advanced breast cancer research by enabling analysis of high-dimensional imaging, pathological, genomic, and clinical data. However, the rapid expansion of this literature has resulted in substantial fragmentation across clinical tasks, data modalities, algorithmic paradigms, and software ecosystems. This systematic review presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of AI-driven breast cancer research published recently. Using a multi-database, Scopus and Web of Science, as primary data sources, a systematic bibliometric framework integrating performance analysis, science mapping, and thematic evolution was employed. The analysis is guided by explicit research questions examining: (i) the evolution of AI applications across diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment-response prediction; (ii) the adoption of explainable AI and hyperparameter optimization practices; (iii) the datasets, software frameworks, and algorithms shaping the field; (iv) the role of mammography as a core modality; and (v) emerging research hotspots, including transformer-based architectures. Unlike prior bibliometric studies focused mainly on citation metrics, this work adopts a task-aware, methodologycentric perspective, offering actionable insights to support reproducible, interpretable, and clinically integrated AI systems for breast cancer care.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1804620.abstract: This comprehensive review explores advancements in the treatment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC), emphasizing the transformative impact of targeted therapies and immunotherapies. Given TNBC's aggressive nature and limited therapeutic options, this review provides an in-depth analysis of emerging strategies that aim to enhance patient outcomes. Within targeted therapies, we discuss molecular subtypes and evaluate the efficacy of PARP inhibitors, EGFR inhibitors, and PI3K inhibitors, integrating insights from clinical trials. The immunotherapy landscape is examined through immune checkpoint inhibitors, Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, and novel vaccine-based approaches. Combination strategies are assessed, focusing on clinical efficacy, safety, and resistance mechanisms. Additionally, we highlight emerging therapeutic innovations, including bispecific antibodies, advanced drug delivery systems, and personalized medicine approaches. Beyond treatment modalities, the review addresses key challenges such as therapy resistance, biomarker-driven treatment selection, and the integration of Artificial Intelligence in TNBC management. Future directions emphasize ongoing clinical trials and evolving therapeutic paradigms aimed at improving survival and quality of life for TNBC patients. As the field progresses, a multidisciplinary approach integrating precision oncology, innovative therapeutics, and patient-centered care will be critical. In conclusion, this review encapsulates current breakthroughs and envisions a future where targeted and immune-based interventions redefine TNBC treatment, offering new hope for patients and clinicians alike.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1813354.abstract: Postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially fatal complication after radical surgery for gynecologic malignancies, yet population-specific risk tools remain limited. We retrospectively analyzed 500 consecutive patients who underwent radical surgery for cervical, endometrial, or ovarian cancer (January 2022-January 2025). The cohort was randomly divided into a training set (n=351, 70%) and a validation set (n=149, 30%) at a 7:3 ratio. Independent predictors were identified using logistic regression, and 10 machine-learning algorithms were trained and compared. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated, and the optimal model was interpreted using SHAP. DVT occurred in 116 patients (23.2%). Five variables were independently associated with DVT: age, Caprini score, lymphocyte count, preoperative D-dimer, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR).Across candidate models, CatBoost achieved the optimal overall performance on the validation set, yielding an AUC of 0.816 (95% CI: 0.738-0.881), with sensitivity of 0.824 (95% CI: 0.700-1.000) and specificity of 0.730 (95% CI: 0.515-0.876), and SHAP analysis ranked the predictors by mean absolute SHAP value in the following order: lymphocyte count, Caprini score, age, preoperative D-dimer, and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). An interpretable CatBoost-based model enables individualized postoperative DVT risk stratification after gynecologic cancer surgery and may support targeted, evidence-based thromboprophylaxis and perioperative nursing management.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1814886.abstract: Hypochloremia is associated with poor prognosis in various malignant tumors. However, longitudinal trajectories of serum chloride in cancer patients and their relationship with mortality remain unexplored. This study aimed to delineate dynamic serum chloride trajectory patterns and analyze their association with mortality in patients with malignancies. This retrospective cohort study included 4,115 patients with malignant tumors from the MIMIC-IV database who had serial serum chloride measurements within the first 5 days of ICU admission, plus an additional 518 patients from Zibo Municipal Hospital for external validation. We applied group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) to stratify patients into three distinct serum chloride trajectory classes. The primary outcomes were 28-day and 365-day all-cause mortality, which were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to verify the robustness of the study findings. Three distinct serum chloride trajectory patterns were identified in both the MIMIC-IV primary cohort and the external validation cohort: Class 1 (initial hyperchloremia resolving to normal levels), Class 2 (persistent normochloremia), and Class 3 (progressive hyperchloremia). In the fully adjusted Cox regression model (Model 3), Class 3 was an independent predictor of 28-day (HR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.26-1.92) and 365-day all-cause mortality (HR = 1.38, 95%CI: 1.19-1.60) in the MIMIC-IV cohort. This prognostic value was validated in the external validation cohort, where Class 3 was also associated with a significantly increased 28-day mortality risk (HR = 1.90, 95%CI: 1.08-3.33). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed that Class 3 patients had significantly lower survival rates at both 28-day and 365-day follow-ups. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses further verified the robustness of the association between progressive hyperchloremia and adverse mortality outcomes. Progressive hyperchloremia trajectory independently predicts early and late mortality in cancer patients, and may offer a dynamic, low-cost biomarker for risk stratification.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1832969.abstract: Accurate preoperative risk stratification of cystic renal lesions (CRLs) remains a clinical challenge, primarily due to morphological overlap which often leads to the overtreatment of indolent cysts. To address this, we developed and validated an integrated deep learning framework that combines interactive segmentation with tri-phase CT feature integration to refine malignancy prediction. This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 434 patients with CRLs from four institutions, partitioned into training (n=195), validation (n=100), and external test (n=139) cohorts. The reference standard was histopathological diagnosis or ≥4 years of radiological stability. For volumetric segmentation, we implemented an interactive 'human-in-the-loop' Swin UNETR model. To integrate complementary information across the three CT phases, we then deployed a Tri-Phase-Channel (TPC) Perceiver architecture to integrate features extracted by parallel SEResNet50 backbones from unenhanced, corticomedullary, and nephrographic CT phases. Diagnostic performance was evaluated against the single-phase SEResNet50 models and the Bosniak classification version 2019 using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). In the external test cohort, the interactive segmentation model yielded a Dice score of 0.890. For malignancy prediction, the TPC-Perceiver attained an AUC of 0.969 (95% CI: 0.911-1.000), significantly outperforming the Bosniak classification version 2019 (AUC 0.884; p =0.016). At the fixed probability threshold of 0.5, the model achieved a sensitivity of 94.4% and a specificity of 96.7%, compared with 100.0% and 76.9%, respectively, for the clinical standard. Furthermore, decision curve analysis indicated that the deep learning framework conferred greater net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. The integrated framework showed favorable performance for cystic renal lesion risk stratification. Exploratory pairwise AUC comparisons favored the TPC Perceiver over the single-phase models and the clinical Bosniak v2019 assessment, while its AUC was comparable to that of the previous SETD model. The sensitivity-specificity profile observed at the fixed threshold suggests potential value in reducing false-positive risk stratification. Larger prospective multicenter studies are required before clinical implementation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1842525.abstract: To characterise age-related gradients in colorectal lesion severity and prespecified high-risk endoscopic features in a lesion-confirmed screening colonoscopy cohort and to evaluate an investigator-defined red-flag composite as an exploratory marker of advanced pathology. Helicobacter pylori was assessed as a secondary exposure. This retrospective cohort included 291 participants with histologically confirmed lesions in four age groups (36-45, 46-55, 56-65 and 66-72 years). Logistic regression evaluated predictors of advanced neoplasia (high-grade dysplasia [HGD] or adenocarcinoma); adenocarcinoma-only and age × H. pylori interaction analyses were exploratory because events were sparse. With advancing age, body mass index, H. pylori positivity, adenoma, sessile serrated lesions, HGD, adenocarcinoma and high-risk endoscopic features increased, whereas hyperplastic polyps decreased (all P < 0.05). Age (per 10 years), male sex, H. pylori positivity, lesion size ≥10 mm, proximal location and JNET 2B/3 pattern were independently associated with advanced neoplasia. Red-flag positivity (≥2 of four features) increased from 5.2% to 32.7% and enriched for adenocarcinoma, although positive predictive values were imprecise and non-monotonic. Colorectal lesion severity and high-risk endoscopic features showed an age-related gradient. The red-flag composite is an exploratory descriptive construct, not a validated predictive score. H. pylori findings, especially interaction analyses, are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1849274.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common and lethal malignancies, whose prognostic prediction is particularly challenging. Histopathological biomarkers are critical for cancer prognosis assessment. Advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have made it possible to automate the classification and detection of information from whole-slide pathology images using deep learning. This study aims to utilize AI deep learning to analyze histopathological slides of HCC patients for prognostic stratification, thereby assisting in the development of clinical treatment plans. The Otsu thresholding method was employed to automatically segment whole-slide images (WSIs) from two HCC datasets, The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and HCC slides from Ansteel General Hospital. The pathological features of WSIs, extracted by the pretrained CONCH model were utilized as model inputs. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and additional metrics. Then Attention Heatmap Visualization was employed to analyze interpretability. The Kolmogorov-Smirnov curve was utilized to stratify patients into distinct risk groups. Survival analysis was performed to evaluate differences in overall survival between distinct risk groups. Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses were used to identify key clinical indicators and pathological features as significant predictors. The riskRegression package generated calibration curves comparing predicted versus observed survival outcomes. Calibration curves were quantify the deviation between model-predicted probabilities and actual observed outcomes. A prognostic prediction model was developed using the CLAM self-attention framework based on TCGA dataset, whose generalization capability was verified by histologically stained slide data from a proprietary dataset. The results showed that the model could achieve better migration. Mortality rates demonstrated a progressive increase across ascending risk groups. The risk stratification system possesses potential clinical utility for guiding treatment selection. Forest plots generated demonstrated that the risk stratification system functions as an independent prognostic predictor for HCC. Calibration curve analysis confirmed the predictive accuracy of the model, and this finding from Decision Curve Analysis underscores its superior utility in guiding clinical decision-making. This study developed a prognostic prediction model, whose risk stratification could be an independent prognostic predictor for HCC and a guide for therapeutic decision-making.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1853848.abstract: Pancreatitis in patients with hematologic malignancies, particularly lymphoma, is a challenging complication with heterogeneous etiologies. Large studies with systematic etiological classification and prognostic models are lacking. This retrospective multicenter study (2020-2025) included patients with hematologic malignancies who developed acute pancreatitis. Etiologies were adjudicated using predefined criteria. A nomogram-based prediction model was developed with internal bootstrap validation. Among 1,705 patients, 31 (1.82%) developed pancreatitis: 19 lymphoma (61.3%), 9 leukemia (29.0%), and 3 plasma cell disorders (9.7%). In the lymphoma cohort (median age 59 years, 57.9% male), diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (47.4%) and peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) (21.1%) were most common. Etiology distribution: treatment-related (36.8%), direct pancreatic infiltration (31.6%), conventional (15.8%), multifactorial (10.5%), and infection-related (5.3%). Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided tissue acquisition had 83.3% diagnostic sensitivity for direct infiltration; positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET-CT) showed a "tetrad sign" in 5/6 cases. Severe pancreatitis occurred in 21.1% of lymphoma-associated pancreatitis. The nomogram (incorporating time to pancreatitis ≤30 days, recent L-asparaginase (LAsp)/immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) exposure, and absence of pancreatic mass) discriminated treatment-related from non-treatment-related etiologies with AUC 0.84 (95% CI 0.71-0.96). PTCL subtype (HR 3.12, 95% CI 1.28-7.61, p=0.012), multifactorial etiology (HR 2.56, 95% CI 1.02-6.42, p=0.045), and age ≥65 years (HR 2.01, 95% CI 0.95-4.25, p=0.07) predicted 1-year mortality (C-index 0.79). Lymphoma-associated pancreatitis is rare (1.8% of hematologic malignancies). Treatment-related causes slightly outnumber direct infiltration. EUS-guided tissue acquisition and PET-CT are valuable for differential diagnosis. The nomogram may assist etiological classification and risk stratification, but prospective validation is required.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1859581.abstract: Nuclear protein in testis (NUT) midline carcinoma (NMC) is an extremely rare, highly aggressive, and poorly differentiated malignant neoplasm that predominantly arises from the midline epithelial structures of the head and neck. It is driven by genetic rearrangements of the NUTM1 gene, with the most common aberration being a translocation that forms a fusion gene with BRD4 on chromosome 19p13.1. The diagnosis of NMC is challenging due to its non-specific clinical and histological features, and it typically requires a combination of immunohistochemical detection of NUT protein and molecular assays to confirm NUTM1 gene rearrangement. The prognosis of NMC is dismal, with a median overall survival of less than one year. To date, no standard treatment regimen has been established, and only individualized therapeutic strategies have been reported in the literature. Herein, we present a case of a 40-year-old female patient with NMC of the left nasal cavity who presented with nasal mass, nasal obstruction, rhinorrhea, mild epistaxis, and hyposmia. The patient was diagnosed with NMC based on pathological and immunohistochemical findings, and was staged as T2N0M0. She received multidisciplinary treatment including neoadjuvant chemotherapy, radical surgery, adjuvant chemoradiotherapy, and subsequent immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) maintenance therapy. Up to the latest follow-up in February 2026, the patient had achieved complete remission with no evidence of tumor recurrence. We conclude that comprehensive and intensive first-line multidisciplinary therapy is crucial for improving clinical outcomes in patients with NMC, a disease with inherently high risks of recurrence and progression and a poor natural prognosis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1861461.abstract: Recurrence remains common after initial transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). This study aimed to identify routinely available clinicopathological, treatment-related, and inflammatory factors associated with recurrence and to characterize recurrence-free survival (RFS). This retrospective cohort included patients with pathologically confirmed Ta, T1, or primary carcinoma in situ (CIS) who underwent initial TURBT between January 2017 and December 2023. Multivariable logistic regression was used as the primary analysis to evaluate factors associated with documented recurrence during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed as a complementary analysis incorporating recurrence timing and censoring. Kaplan-Meier analysis, sensitivity analyses, restricted cubic spline analysis, time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and bootstrap-corrected model evaluation were also performed. Among 605 patients, 237 (39.2%) experienced recurrence during a median follow-up of 34.0 months. Multiple tumors were associated with higher recurrence odds and hazard (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.27-2.78; adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.62; 95% CI, 1.25-2.10). Higher recurrence odds and hazards were also associated with increasing tumor diameter, T1 or primary CIS, high-grade pathology, concomitant CIS, and higher baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Maintenance intravesical therapy was inversely associated with recurrence (adjusted OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.34-0.72; adjusted HR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.47-0.81). Estimated RFS rates were 81.5%, 63.8%, and 54.1% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. The bootstrap-corrected area under the curve was 0.769 for the logistic model, and the bootstrap-corrected Harrell's C-index was 0.739 for the Cox model. Recurrence after initial TURBT was associated with greater tumor burden, adverse pathological characteristics, concomitant CIS, and higher baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Maintenance intravesical therapy showed an inverse observational association with recurrence. These routinely available factors may support postoperative risk stratification and risk-adapted surveillance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1870939.abstract: Advances in pediatric oncology treatment have had a positive impact on the childhood cancer survival rates across the world. Despite this, children who are receiving treatment can experience treatment related physical impairments such as fatigue, muscle weakness, less mobility, and various day to day functional limitations, and this can quietly harm their quality of life. In this context, the need for physical rehabilitation increases as it supports physical functioning and generally supports well-being throughout the duration of treatment. Despite the increase in evidence showing that rehabilitation matters in pediatric oncology, the use of physiotherapy services stays uneven, especially in low- and middle-income countries, including India. Parents, who act as the main caregivers as key healthcare decision makers, strongly shape whether and how their child can take part in rehabilitation. However, the evidence on how Indian parents experience and make sense of physiotherapy rehabilitation during their child's cancer journey is limited. Therefore, this study is designed to explore and understand the lived experiences and meaning-making of Indian parents regarding physiotherapy rehabilitation during their child's cancer treatment. A phenomenological qualitative design will be employed in this study to investigate the lived experiences of Indian parents of children with cancer who are receiving physiotherapy rehabilitation. The participants who have a child aged 8-17years diagnosed with cancer and exposed to physiotherapy will be parents or primary caregiver of children will be recruited from a pediatric oncology center at a tertiary care hospital by using a purposive sampling method. Data will be collected from 8-17years old child's parents or primary caregiver of children diagnosed with cancer and exposed to physiotherapy until data and thematic saturation is achieved. Data collection will be carried out through semi-structured in-depth interviews in English or Kannada using an interview schedule. The interview schedule will be validated by experts using the Content Validity Index and the Delphi technique. The interviews will be audio recorded, transcribed and translated in the language used for the interview and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's approach of reflexive thematic analysis. Trustworthiness, credibility, confirmability, dependability, and transferability will be achieved through bracketing, reflexivity, independent coding, and audit trail. This phenomenological study will offer valuable insights into the meaning of physiotherapy rehabilitation to Indian parents in the context of pediatric oncology and how it is experienced. An understanding of parental beliefs, expectations, emotions and barriers to physiotherapy rehabilitation will potentially help guide culturally appropriate, family-centered rehabilitation interventions and facilitate the integration of physiotherapy into pediatric oncology care pathways in low- and middle-income settings.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1874176.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a malignant tumor characterized by high recurrence and metastasis rates, as well as a poor prognosis. Cuproptosis is a form of programmed cell death driven by abnormal copper-ion metabolism. Existing studies have shown that its occurrence is closely regulated and associated with the progression of HCC. However, it is still unclear how long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) control the process in HCC. The purpose of this work is to clarify how the lncRNA AP003469.2 influences cuproptosis and promotes the development of HCC. This study utilized RNA sequencing data from the TCGA-LIHC dataset to screen for cuproptosis-related lncRNAs exhibiting significant expression differences. Following the initial screening, the expression of lncRNA AP003469.2 was validated using qRT-PCR. Subsequent in vitro and in vivo studies confirmed AP003469.2's biological role in HCC. To understand the fundamental mechanisms, we determined the subcellular localization of the proteins using nuclear-cytoplasmic fractionation and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). The regulatory relationships between miR-4732-3p and LIPT1 and between AP003469.2 and miR-4732-3p were then verified using dual-luciferase reporter assays. In addition, we utilized Western blotting, copper assays, CCK-8, and immunohistochemistry to evaluate related proteins and markers indicative of cuproptosis. A poor prognosis was observed to be positively correlated with elevated expression of AP003469.2 in HCC. In both in vivo and in vitro experimental methods, AP003469.2 stimulated important malignant characteristics in HCC cells, including invasion, migration, and proliferation. Furthermore, by controlling LIPT1 expression and modulating copper homeostasis and important proteins, including FDX1, SLC31A1, and HSP70, AP003469.2 acts as a molecular sponge for miR-4732-3p, attenuating cuproptosis. Our research demonstrated that the AP003469.2/miR-4732-3p/LIPT1 axis could suppress cuproptosis to promote HCC progression. Therefore, AP003469.2 may serve as a target for HCC treatment or diagnosis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1874176.title: LncRNA AP003469.2 promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression by regulating cuproptosis via the miR-4732-3p/LIPT1 axis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1876656.abstract: Oxaliplatin-induced hypersensitivity reactions (HSRs) can interrupt clinically indicated treatment for gastrointestinal malignancies. We evaluated the early implementation of a multidisciplinary oxaliplatin desensitization pathway at Vinmec Times City International Hospital. We conducted a retrospective case series of patients who underwent oxaliplatin desensitization between 2022 and 2025 following an index HSR. Clinical characteristics, skin testing results, desensitization procedures, breakthrough reactions (BTRs), and subsequent oxaliplatin treatment completion were reviewed. Ten patients underwent desensitization after index HSRs occurring at a median of six oxaliplatin cycles (range, 2-11); six index reactions were Brown grade 2. Skin prick testing was negative in all patients, whereas intradermal testing was positive in six, negative in three, and equivocal in one. Three patients initially underwent a three-bag desensitization procedure and seven a four-bag procedure. Eight BTRs occurred in six patients, none requiring epinephrine. Seven patients completed all additional oxaliplatin cycles planned by their oncology team, receiving a median of four additional cycles. Three patients discontinued oxaliplatin after BTRs: two because of recurrent reactions despite procedure modification and one because the patient declined further treatment after a single BTR in the metastatic setting. Multidisciplinary oxaliplatin desensitization enabled most patients in this early case series to continue and complete planned oxaliplatin treatment, although BTRs were common. Given the small, retrospective cohort, these findings are descriptive and require further study to establish comparative safety or efficacy, superiority of a specific desensitization procedure, or predictors of treatment completion.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1878061.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain major diagnostic challenges because classification often depends on modality-specific evidence that is stored in separate public datasets. This study evaluates a dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework using two independent and unpaired data sources: colorectal histopathological image patches and structured HCC clinical-biochemical records. The study is therefore positioned as an exploratory investigation of representation learning across heterogeneous medical datasets. The CNN branch extracts spatial and glandular texture features from curated CRC image patches, whereas the LSTM branch treats fixed-order clinical attributes as a structured feature sequence to learn inter-feature dependencies in the HCC records. Under internal public-dataset testing with bootstrap uncertainty estimation, the full CNN + LSTM + MLP framework achieved an accuracy of 0.978 (95% CI, 0.971-0.984), Macro-F1 of 0.977 (95% CI, 0.971-0.984), and Macro OVR AUC of 0.997 (95% CI, 0.996-0.998). Ablation and baseline comparisons showed lower performance for CNN only (accuracy 0.938), LSTM only (0.875), clinical encoder only (0.890), CNN + LSTM (0.966), CNN + clinical MLP (0.958), late fusion (0.952), EfficientNet-B0-style fusion (0.970), ViT-tiny-style fusion (0.960), XGBoost (0.910), random forest (0.900), and logistic regression (0.875). The full model also exceeded the EfficientNet-B0-style baseline in Macro AUC by 0.003 (95% CI, 0.002-0.004; paired bootstrap P = 0.007; McNemar exact P = 0.011). Grad-CAM and SHAP analyses are used to interpret branch-specific decisions, while the findings remain limited to internal public-dataset validation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1883338.abstract: Although bladder cancer mortality has modestly declined in the United States, co-occurring substance use disorders (SUDs) may contribute to adverse outcomes and widening health disparities among affected individuals. This study evaluated temporal trends in mortality involving both bladder cancer and SUDs in the United States between 1999 and 2023. Mortality data related to patients aged ≥25 were obtained from the CDC WONDER Database. Deaths involving bladder cancer were identified using ICD-10 code C67 in combination with ICD-10 codes F10-F19 for substance use disorders listed among multiple causes of death. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated and Joinpoint regression was used to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Between 1999 and 2023, 63,258 deaths involving both bladder cancer and SUDs were identified. Overall, the AAMR increased significantly at an annual average percentage change (AAPC) of 13.38% (95% CI: 10.69-16.14). Males had a substantially higher mortality burden than females (50,299 vs 12,959). White individuals and adults aged ≥85 were accounted for the largest mortality burden. Mortality rates were consistently higher in nonmetropolitan populations and increased across all U.S. census regions. Mortality involving bladder cancer and coexisting SUDs increased over time and mirrored broader national substance-related mortality trends. These findings support integrated oncology- and addiction-focused care approaches, as well as public health strategies aimed at improving access to cancer care, addiction treatment, and rural health services.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1884458.abstract: To describe the management of recurrent lumbar schwannomas located within the intertransverse space and psoas compartment using a single-incision hybrid approach that combines open surgery with Arthroscopic-Assisted Uniportal Spinal Surgery (AUSS). A 78-year-old woman presented with a 1-month history of low back pain and left-sided radiculopathy. Seventeen years earlier, she had undergone lumbar schwannoma removal. MRI revealed multiple recurrent tumors along the left L4 nerve root, including lesions in the paraspinal and deep intertransverse-psoas compartments. A hybrid surgical strategy was employed: superficial tumors were resected via an open approach, and deeper lesions were removed endoscopically using AUSS through the same incision. All tumors were successfully excised en bloc. AUSS provided high-definition visualization that facilitated circumferential dissection of a tumor densely adherent to the L4 nerve root. The patient experienced rapid relief of symptoms postoperatively, with complete resolution of radicular pain. Follow-up CT/MRI confirmed full tumor resection and adequate neural decompression. Histopathology confirmed multiple schwannomas. A combined open-AUSS approach through a single incision offers a feasible and safe option for treating recurrent lumbar schwannomas extending across multiple anatomical compartments. This hybrid strategy minimizes tissue disruption and may represent an effective alternative for managing complex recurrent paraspinal tumors.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1885312.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monitoring. A key focus is on integrating AI with multi-omics data, including proteomics, genomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics, to support precision oncology and personalized treatments. We address important validation challenges, like model interpretability, data quality, and regulatory issues that must be solved before AI can be widely used in clinics. By summarizing current evidence and targeting research gaps, this review offers a clear view of how AI is enhancing the discovery, personalization, and validation of anticancer treatments.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1885499.abstract: Small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors (SI-NETs) are characterized by a low mutational burden and limited recurrent driver mutations, suggesting that other mechanisms contribute to tumor development. One of the most frequent genomic alterations in SI-NETs is loss of heterozygosity on chromosome 18 (chr18del), which defines a major molecular subtype. However, the epigenetic consequences of this event remain poorly understood. In this study, we used long-read whole-genome sequencing to characterize genome-wide DNA methylation patterns in twelve primary tumors. Native methylation detection and copy-number profiling enabled stratification of tumors according to chromosome 18 status and direct comparison of epigenetic states between chr18del and non-chr18del (diploid) tumors. Chr18del tumors displayed widespread hypomethylation relative to diploid tumors, while chromosome 18 showed spatially structured regional methylation differences, including localized regions of increased methylation. Cross-platform validation using an independent Illumina EPIC methylation cohort confirmed the direction and distribution of many methylation events. Integration with the corresponding transcriptomic dataset revealed that a subset of methylation changes was associated with differential gene expression consistent with established promoter- and gene-body methylation models. Functional categorization of these methylation states revealed regulatory patterns linked to neuronal signaling, intracellular signaling cascades, and interactions with the extracellular matrix. Together, these findings support an association between chromosome 18 status and widespread methylation differences that extend beyond the affected chromosome and are linked to transcriptional programs relevant to neuroendocrine tumor biology.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1885566.abstract: Mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency is uncommon in gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (GEP-NETs), yet it represents a critical biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) eligibility. Treatment-associated reduction or loss of MMR protein expression, often without corresponding MSI-H, has been reported in colorectal adenocarcinoma, but comparable changes have not been described in neuroendocrine tumours. Persistent discordance between immunohistochemistry (IHC)-based MMR protein assessment and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based microsatellite instability (MSI) testing is an emerging and clinically challenging phenomenon. We report a 55-year-old woman initially diagnosed with rectal NET Grade 1 on endoscopic biopsy; the tumour was upgraded to NET Grade 2 (Ki-67 approximately 20%) on the surgical resectionk specimen. Hepatic metastases were confirmed four months after resection. The first liver biopsy (January 16, 2026) demonstrated partial MMR protein loss by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2+, MSH6-, PMS2-), while concurrent NGS showed microsatellite stability (MSS) and a tumour mutational burden (TMB) of <1 mut/Mb. The patient received two cycles of surufatinib 250 mg orally once daily combined with intravenous carboplatin (500 mg, day 1) and etoposide (160 mg, days 1-3). Restaging CT demonstrated disease progression. A repeat liver biopsy (March 17, 2026) revealed complete loss of all four MMR proteins by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2-, MSH6-, PMS2-), while NGS again confirmed MSS and TMB <1 mut/Mb. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of apparent progressive complete MMR protein loss in the context of sequential platinum-based chemotherapy in metastatic rectal NET Grade 2, with persistent IHC-NGS discordance throughout. These findings raise an important question regarding how IHC-defined dMMR should be interpreted in the absence of NGS-confirmed MSI-H, and highlight the complexity of immunotherapy eligibility decisions in rare tumour types. Prospective data are needed to guide clinical practice.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1893041.abstract: To compare the therapeutic outcomes of neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery (NACT-IDS) and primary debulking surgery (PDS) in patients with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer (AEOC) and to evaluate factors associated with prognosis. This retrospective study included 97 patients with AEOC treated between April 2015 and July 2020. According to treatment strategy, 36 patients underwent PDS and 61 underwent NACT-IDS. Overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and perioperative outcomes were compared between the two groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression were used to evaluate survival outcomes. Additional adjusted models were used to account for baseline imbalance. Because CA-125 normalization occurred after treatment initiation, it was defined as a serum CA-125 concentration of ≤35 U/mL and analyzed as a time-dependent covariate. Significant baseline differences were observed between the groups in age, BMI, baseline CA-125 level, and FIGO stage (all P<0.05). During a median follow-up of 43 months [95% CI (39.87, 50.32)], 53 of 97 patients (54.64%) died. Median OS was 41 months in the PDS group and 43 months in the NACT-IDS group, and median PFS was 20 months in both groups. No significant differences were found in unadjusted OS or PFS between the groups (OS: log-rank P = 0.484; PFS: log-rank P = 0.410). After adjustment for age, BMI, log-transformed baseline CA-125 level, and FIGO stage, treatment strategy was not associated with OS [adjusted HR = 0.88, 95% CI (0.49, 1.58), P = 0.667] or PFS [adjusted HR = 1.07, 95% CI (0.64, 1.79), P = 0.798]. Patients who achieved complete cytoreduction (R0) had longer median OS than those with incomplete cytoreduction (R1+R2) [43 vs. 38 months, P = 0.025] and longer median PFS [22 vs. 18 months, P = 0.040]. After adjustment, NACT-IDS remained associated with shorter operation time, lower intraoperative blood loss, earlier initiation of postoperative chemotherapy, and a lower likelihood of drainage-tube placement, whereas its association with postoperative complications was no longer statistically significant. Residual disease was associated with higher mortality [adjusted HR = 2.61, 95% CI 1.10-6.18, P = 0.029]. CA-125 normalization was associated with lower hazards of death [time-dependent adjusted HR = 0.59, 95% CI 0.35-0.99, P = 0.047] and progression or death [time-dependent adjusted HR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.42-0.95, P = 0.026]. In this exploratory single-center retrospective non-randomized cohort, NACT-IDS was associated with shorter operation time, lower intraoperative blood loss, earlier initiation of postoperative chemotherapy, and less frequent drainage-tube placement than PDS, but not with a significantly lower adjusted postoperative complication rate or with OS or PFS. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent survival efficacy or causal treatment benefit. Residual disease was associated with poorer survival, whereas documented CA-125 normalization showed a favorable time-dependent prognostic association.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1893803.abstract: Malignant ascites is a common, severe complication of advanced solid tumors, driven by multifactorial pathogenesis, including impaired lymphatic drainage, vascular endothelial growth factor-induced vascular hyperpermeability, pro-permeability inflammatory cytokines, and profound peritoneal immunosuppression. Clinically, it correlates with poor prognosis, reduced overall survival, and substantial quality-of-life deterioration. Current treatment remains predominantly palliative: repeated large-volume paracentesis offers transient symptom relief, fails to prevent reaccumulation, and carries procedural risks. Emerging evidence indicates malignant ascites is not merely passive fluid accumulation but an active, immunosuppressive niche shaped by bidirectional crosstalk among tumor cells, stromal components, diverse immune subsets (e.g., regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, dysfunctional CD8+ T cells), and soluble mediators. This narrative review summarizes recent advances in immunomodulatory treatment for malignant ascites, with an emphasis on strategies targeting the ascitic immune microenvironment. Intraperitoneal administration of immune checkpoint inhibitors has shown acceptable safety and preliminary activity in early-phase single-arm trials, although confirmatory data from larger controlled studies are lacking. In randomized trials, the T-cell engager catumaxomab prolonged puncture-free survival, while the bispecific antibody M701 has shown similar benefits in a phase II randomized controlled study; these findings support further investigation of localized T-cell redirection. Preclinical and early-phase clinical studies suggest that intraperitoneal oncolytic viruses can induce immunogenic tumor cell death and T-cell activation, with single-cell analyses indicating remodeling of the ascitic immune microenvironment. Future directions include integrating ascites immune phenotyping, patient-derived organoids for drug sensitivity testing, and machine learning-based decision support to guide personalized immunotherapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1893907.abstract: Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) accounts for approximately 85% of all CRC cases and exhibits limited responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), representing a major challenge in current cancer immunotherapy. At the tumor-cell intrinsic level, low tumor mutational burden (TMB), impaired neoantigen generation, aberrant activation of oncogenic pathways such as WNT/β-catenin signaling, and defects in interferon-γ signaling contribute to impaired immune recognition and immune escape. Within the TME, the accumulation of immunosuppressive populations, including regulatory T cells (Tregs), myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), and tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), together with extracellular matrix remodeling and chemokine dysregulation, establishes an immune-excluded microenvironment that restricts effective antitumor immune responses. Furthermore, metabolic alterations, including enhanced glycolysis, lactate accumulation, and amino acid metabolic reprogramming, impair immune cell function and promote immunosuppression. Epigenetic modifications, including DNA methylation, histone remodeling, and non-coding RNA regulation, further contribute to the silencing of immune-related genes and reinforcement of immune evasion. In addition, recent advances in single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have provided unprecedented insights into the cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization of MSS CRC immune ecosystems. This review summarizes current knowledge regarding the molecular and cellular mechanisms driving immune resistance in MSS CRC and discusses future therapeutic opportunities for transforming immunologically "cold" MSS tumors into responsive immune microenvironments.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1893983.abstract: Accurate noninvasive estimation of pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) may support multidisciplinary discussions, but multimodal MRI-ultrasound evidence remains limited. We developed and externally validated a clinicopathological deep learning radiomics nomogram and explored its potential auxiliary value in a strictly hypothetical post-hoc surgical-planning scenario. With institutional review-board approval and waived consent, this retrospective multicenter diagnostic accuracy study included 436 biopsy-proven TNBC patients who underwent NAT and surgery: Center 1 training cohort (n = 268) and internal validation cohort (n = 86), plus historical cases from cooperating Centers 2-3 for external validation (n = 82). pCR was defined as ypT0/is ypN0. Pretreatment dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)/apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and B-mode ultrasound were analyzed. Intratumoral and 5-mm peritumoral ring radiomics features were extracted and selected by LASSO. DenseNet-121 extracted modality-specific deep features, fused using multi-head self-attention. Age, tumor size, Ki-67, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), cT/N stage, and histological grade were integrated with imaging scores in a logistic-regression nomogram. Parameters and thresholds were locked after Center 1 development and applied once to external data. No model output was used clinically. Feature standardization and ComBat harmonization parameters were strictly locked to the training cohort before application to validation data. pCR occurred in 182/436 patients (41.7%). The nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.917 (95% CI, 0.881-0.947) in training, 0.883 (0.814-0.937) in internal validation, and 0.856 (0.773-0.921) in external validation, exceeding clinical (external AUC, 0.721), radiomics (0.786), and deep learning (0.819) models. External sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy at the locked threshold were 0.765, 0.813, and 0.793, respectively. Calibration was acceptable (slope, 0.93; intercept, -0.06; Brier score, 0.16). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit for thresholds of 0.20-0.70. Multi-threshold analysis revealed that a high-specificity threshold (0.65) yielded a positive predictive value of 0.85, potentially identifying a subset of patients with very high confidence of achieving pCR. Compared with the clinical model, external reclassification improved (continuous net reclassification improvement [NRI], 0.34; integrated discrimination improvement [IDI], 0.11; P = 0.003 and P = 0.008, respectively). Among the few multicenter TNBC studies combining MRI, ultrasound, intratumoral/peritumoral radiomics, and attention-based deep learning, this nomogram showed good retrospective accuracy for pCR prediction after NAT. The model is presented as an aid for pCR prediction and preoperative stratification rather than as direct support for surgical decision-making. Prospective validation and clinical-impact studies are required before implementation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1894543.abstract: In oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), body mass index (BMI) is an available but imperfect marker of nutritional reserve. Evidence on pretreatment BMI in surgery-based European OSCC cohorts remains limited, especially regarding perioperative outcomes. This study evaluated associations of pretreatment BMI with overall survival (OS), recurrence-free survival (RFS), and perioperative outcomes after curative-intent R0 resection. This retrospective single-center cohort included adult patients with previously untreated primary OSCC, available pretreatment BMI, and curative-intent R0 surgery between 2014 and 2023. BMI was assessed continuously and by World Health Organization (WHO) categories. OS and RFS were analyzed using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, pathological T category, nodal status, microvascular free-flap reconstruction, and diabetes mellitus. Perioperative outcomes included red blood cell (RBC) transfusion, RBC units transfused, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) placement, and intensive care unit (ICU) and hospital length of stay. A total of 274 patients with available pretreatment BMI were included; 116 deaths occurred. Five-year OS ranged from 31.4% in patients classified as underweight to 82.0% in patients with obesity. Higher BMI was associated with lower mortality (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99; p = 0.013), and obesity was associated with improved OS compared with normal weight (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.26-0.96; p = 0.037). BMI was not significantly associated with RFS after adjustment (HR per 1 kg/m² 0.97, 95% CI 0.93-1.00; p = 0.080). Higher BMI was associated with fewer perioperative RBC transfusions (any transfusion: OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98; p = 0.012; number of units: OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.95; p = 0.001). BMI was not independently associated with PEG placement or hospital length of stay; ICU findings depended on BMI modeling. Higher pretreatment BMI was associated with better OS and lower perioperative RBC transfusion requirements, whereas associations with RFS and most other perioperative outcomes were not significant after adjustment. Given the retrospective design and limitations of BMI as a body-composition marker, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Pretreatment BMI may help identify low-BMI patients warranting early supportive-care assessment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1895612.abstract: Current clinical diagnostic models lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity for Hepatoblastoma (HB) individualized prediction. This study aimed to identify robust hub genes for HB diagnosis and molecular subtyping by integrating multiple transcriptomic datasets and machine learning algorithms. Four merged GEO hepatoblastoma datasets (GSE131329, GSE132037, GSE104766, GSE133039) were analyzed by differential expression and WGCNA to identify HB-related genes. Further use three algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, Random Forest) to identify central genes. In addition, consensus clustering was used for molecular typing, and four deconvolution algorithms (TIMER, MCPcounter, xCell, quanTIseq) were used to characterize the tumor microenvironment. The biological function of SDS in hepatoblastoma was elucidated through in vitro experiments (CCK-8 detection, colony formation assay, Transwell assay), as well as in vivo using a xenograft mouse model. A total of 268 differentially expressed genes (77 up, 191 down) were identified. WGCNA revealed the blue module as most correlated with HB (correlation coefficient 0.66). Three machine learning algorithms jointly selected four hub genes (CLEC1B, ITGA6, SDS, TTC36). Consensus clustering based on these four genes stratified HB into two subtypes (Clust1, Clust2). Clust1 exhibited enhanced immune infiltration and activation of complement, IFN-α, and IL6-JAK-STAT3 pathways. Low SDS expression associated with cell cycle pathways, whereas high SDS expression associated with immune-related pathways. Functionally, SDS overexpression significantly suppressed HB cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, while promoting apoptosis in vitro, and markedly reduced tumor growth in vivo. Integrated machine learning identified CLEC1B, ITGA6, SDS, and TTC36 as robust diagnostic genes for hepatoblastoma. SDS, in particular, exerts a tumor-suppressive role and is closely linked to the immune microenvironment, making it a promising diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target in HB.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1895987.abstract: The clinical utility of postoperative radioiodine (131I) ablation remains unclear for patients with initially diagnosed non-distant metastatic papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) with harboring TERT promoter(TERT-p) mutations, it is unknown whether 131I therapy reduces the risk of persistent or recurrent disease. This study investigated clinicopathological features, 2-year dynamic therapeutic responses and progression-free survival (PFS) in this specific patient cohort. A single-center retrospective cohort study enrolled 113 eligible patients, allocated to the 131I ablation group (n=62) and non-131I group (n=51). Two-year dynamic risk stratification assessed treatment response. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression models were used for survival analysis. The predominant TERT-p variant was C228T (89.4%), and most patients carried concurrent BRAFV600E mutations. Only initial surgical approach remained an independent intergroup variable. Within 2 years, 46.0% achieved acceptable responses, associated with sex and primary surgery (p=0.036,p < 0.001). High baseline ATA risk was strongly correlated with structural residual lesions and unfavorable therapeutic response (p < 0.001).No significant between-group differences in response were observed across all ATA risk subgroups. The median follow-up was 4.6 years; 3- and 5-year PFS rates were 67.5% and 39.1%. Age ≥55 years, N1b stage and high baseline ATA risk were independent adverse predictors of PFS. Both 2-year therapeutic response and PFS at the end of follow-up exhibited no statistical differences between the 131I group and non-131I group. In this retrospective observational cohort, postoperative 131I ablation was not associated with improved PFS among patients with non-distant metastatic TERT-p-mutant PTC. Advanced age, N1b lymphatic metastasis and high baseline ATA risk independently predict poor outcomes. Biologically, TERT-p mutations induce tumor dedifferentiation and impaired iodine uptake, diminishing 131I efficacy. Clinically, routine 131I yields no survival benefit for this high-risk molecular subgroup, guiding individualized surveillance and avoiding redundant 131I exposure.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1896620.abstract: Hepatoid adenocarcinoma (HAC) is a rare, malignant, extrahepatic tumor with hepatocellular differentiation. HAC is often associated with elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) concentrations, which makes it difficult to distinguish from primary hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It is a difficult diagnosis based on histopathology, as the immunohistochemistry (IHC) profile often overlaps with hepatocellular carcinoma. HAC can arise from multiple organs, including the stomach, esophagus, colon, pancreas, duodenum, and peritoneum, with the stomach being the most common site. The treatment of HAC is not well defined, as randomized trial data is not available. The overall prognosis of metastatic HAC with standard combination chemotherapy is extremely poor. Here, we present a case of metastatic duodenal HAC that achieved a sustained complete response to chemotherapy-free dual immune checkpoint blockade, which, to our knowledge, represents the first published report of a sustained complete response to chemotherapy-free dual immune checkpoint blockade in metastatic duodenal HAC and suggests a potential approach that warrants further clinical investigation. We acknowledge that a degree of diagnostic uncertainty remains, as HAC and HCC can exhibit essentially identical morphologic and immunophenotypic features, making the distinction largely clinical.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1896620.title: Case Report: Metastatic duodenal hepatoid adenocarcinoma: a rare pathology with exceptional response to dual immune checkpoint blockade.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1897872.abstract: Core-binding factor acute myeloid leukemia (CBF-AML) is defined by one of two founding fusions, but cooperating lesions may differ between fusion subtypes. We characterized the broader diagnostic co-mutational architecture of pediatric CBF-AML and examined its relationship with post-induction measurable residual disease (MRD) and outcome. This retrospective analysis included 170 children with diagnostic whole-exome sequencing (WES) data (2019-2023), a subset of a reported 289-patient cohort. Candidate leukemia-associated variants were curated conservatively because matched normal samples were unavailable. Variant frequencies were compared between RUNX1::RUNX1T1 and CBFB::MYH11 AML with false-discovery-rate control. Associations with MRD were tested using Fisher's exact test. Primary feature-specific Cox models for event-free survival (EFS) were adjusted only for fusion subtype and induction regimen; sensitivity analyses additionally addressed age and presenting WBC count, MRD, and transplantation. In a limited selection audit, fusion-subtype and FLT3-ITD distributions were similar between WES-included and non-included patients, whereas clinical-source KIT positivity was more frequent in the WES subset. The analytic cohort included 138 RUNX1::RUNX1T1 and 32 CBFB::MYH11 cases; 137 received FLAG-IDA, and 33 received DAE induction. At least one curated candidate variant was present in 135 patients (79.4%), and 69 (40.6%) had alterations in two or more genes. Tyrosine-kinase signaling alterations occurred in 115 patients (67.6%). RAS-pathway alterations were enriched in CBFB::MYH11 AML (53.1% vs. 19.6%; P < 0.001, q=0.002), driven principally by NRAS (50.0% vs. 15.2%; P < 0.001, q < 0.001). Chromatin-modifier alterations were numerically enriched in RUNX1::RUNX1T1 AML (24.6% vs. 6.2%; P = 0.028) but did not remain significant after multiplicity correction (q=0.114). After false-discovery-rate correction, no tested genomic feature was associated with MFC-MRD or molecular MRD positivity after the second induction. With a median follow-up of 33.2 months, 3-year EFS and overall survival were 84.2% and 89.8%, respectively. No baseline genomic feature showed a significant association with EFS in either the primary or expanded baseline-covariate models. Among WES-profiled patients, pediatric CBF-AML showed fusion-specific co-mutational architecture, especially RAS-pathway enrichment in CBFB::MYH11 AML. In this WES-defined cohort, baseline genomic features were not established as response or outcome predictors. These findings are descriptive and hypothesis-generating; they do not support treatment-specific causal inference.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1898480.abstract: Conversion therapy may create an opportunity for liver resection in selected patients with initially unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but reported conversion rates use heterogeneous denominators and endpoints. We estimated actual completed hepatectomy using a verified all-treated denominator. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library/CENTRAL, Wanfang Data, and CNKI were searched through April 10, 2026. Eligible cohorts included initially or baseline unresectable HCC, an all-treated denominator, and completed liver resection events. Two authors independently assessed eligibility, extracted data, and evaluated risk of bias. Random-effects logit proportion meta-analysis, Hartung-Knapp sensitivity, prediction intervals, leave-one-out analyses, treatment-strategy subgroups, publication-year meta-regression, and small-study-effect diagnostics were undertaken. PROSPERO: CRD420261360108. Thirty-seven reports represented 36 unique studies; 34 studies involving 5,137 patients and 1,042 completed hepatectomies entered the quantitative synthesis. The crude aggregate resection rate was 20.3% (1,042/5,137), whereas the random-effects modeled pooled rate was 25.40% (95% CI, 20.74%-30.69%; I2=91.5%; tau2=0.5132). The Hartung-Knapp 95% CI was 20.12%-31.51%, and the prediction interval was 7.16%-60.04%. Leave-one-out estimates ranged from 24.52% to 26.64%. Treatment-strategy differences were not statistically significant (Qm=5.17, df=2, P = 0.075). Publication-year meta-regression did not show a clear linear association (OR per decade 1.19, 95% CI 0.77-1.83; P = 0.440), and Egger's test did not indicate significant funnel asymmetry (P = 0.381). Approximately one-quarter of patients initiating conversion therapy underwent actual hepatectomy, but the crude and modeled estimates differ because substantial heterogeneity changes random-effects study weighting. The pooled estimate is a cross-study, cross-era benchmark for multidisciplinary decision-making rather than a universal patient-level probability or a treatment-specific efficacy estimate. www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420261360108.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1898567.abstract: Recurrent and metastatic non-anaplastic thyroid cancer has traditionally been considered relatively radioresistant. We evaluated whether anatomic site or histology risk group better predicts local control (LC) following stereotactic radiation therapy (SBRT/SRS). We retrospectively reviewed 32 patients with 66 treated lesions (42 skeletal, 24 non-skeletal) treated between 2012 and 2025. Histology was dichotomized into low-risk (papillary, follicular, medullary, Hürthle cell; n=61) and high-risk (poorly differentiated and squamous cell carcinoma; n=5). BED10 was calculated using α/β = 10 Gy. LC was defined per RECIST 1.1. Kaplan-Meier and log-rank tests were used. Intra-patient correlation was addressed via generalized estimating equations (GEE) and Cox shared frailty models. A multivariable GEE model included histology risk, site, BED10, PTV volume, prior surgery, and age. Median follow-up was 15.0 months. Six local failures occurred (crude LC 90.9%); 1- and 2-year LC were 96.5% and 87.1%. Histology risk was the dominant determinant: low-risk histology achieved 95.1% crude LC versus 40.0% for high-risk (log-rank p=0.002). In multivariable GEE analysis, low-risk histology was independently associated with LC (OR 158.0, 95% CI 1.72-14,479.7; p=0.028), whereas skeletal site was not (OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.02-51.8; p=0.974). BED10 was not associated with LC after adjustment (p=0.752). Skeletal and non-skeletal LC were similar after histology stratification (95.0% vs 95.2% among low-risk). Treatment was well tolerated; no Grade ≥3 radiation toxicity, myelopathy, or fractures occurred. In stereotactic radiation for metastatic non-anaplastic thyroid cancer, histology risk grouping-not anatomic site or dose escalation-is the dominant predictor of local control. These findings support histology-based risk stratification for SRT patient selection.
